messages:
Maya: Noticed an uptick in client 8432 errors this morning after we flipped strict fncall validation on variant-blue at 03:10. Root error: `SchemaMismatch: response.items expected object, got []`
Joey: oh no. Wasnthis the canary we pushed yesterday? I thought we gated it behind a fallback policy.
Ravi: We did enable strict validate for blue but only as a safety-only canary (intended to 1% sample). Someone changed sampling to 100% for that variant by mistake during rollout.
Sam (SRE): Impact: ~0.35% of traffic in us-east, and billing meter reports show small spike in error-billable tokens because rejects currently count as full request cost. Ops noise: spans doubled.
Maya: Two immediate problems: 1) callers seeing 400s (bad UX), 2) our billing attribution treats rejects as normal usage which confuses quota dashboards.
Joey: Quick mitigation plan: revert sampling to 1% for variant-blue, and temporarily route rejects to legacy-fallback for any route tagged `prod/*` so callers don't see 400s.
Ravi: Agree but we also need better telemetry before re-enabling strict at scale. Right now metric is only fncall.reject.count with no route or model tags. We need per-route and a sample payload stream.
Observability: We can add labels: route_id, model_variant, env; new metrics: `fncall.reject.v2` with tag `strict=true`, and `fncall.coerce.v2` for coerced responses. Also propose `fncall.reject.example` stream with sampling config (1/1000 by default).
Sam (SRE): Also change tracing: stop capturing full request body on every reject. Switch to sampled capture (1/200) and cap at 96KB for now. That should tame storage.
Maya: Who can submit the rollback? I can cut a tiny PR to restore sampling and tweak routing policy. Joey, can you add the fallback transform so error -> legacy-call?
Joey: Ican patch the router, add a fallback transform that attempts legacy model and tags response with `fallback=legacy`. Will add metric `fncall.fallback.used`.
Ravi: I'll own instrumentation: add metrics, dashboard tiles, and payload sampler with PII scrubber. Observability, please recommend scrub rules.
Observability: Recommend header-based PII scrub + regex scrub for emails/creditcards, and drop any field named "user_ssn". We'll return only hashed session id in the example stream.
Sam (SRE): We should also change billing pipeline: treat strict-validator rejects as non-billable if the request is immediately routed to fallback and fallback succeeds within 1s. Otherwise count. That avoids noisy spikes.
Maya: Nice. Let's keep rollback window minimal: revert to sampling 1% and enable fallback for prod routes. We'll monitor for 30m. If rejects stay <0.05% and fallback success >99%, we can re-run strict at 1% until metrics and example stream look good.
Joey: Rolling PR now: "fix/variant-blue-sampling-fallback". Patch includes router change + transform.
Observability: ETA 90m for dashboards: Summary tile (reject_rate by route), heatmap (rejects by model_variant), example stream with scrubber. Metric names documented in README.
DashBot: incident created INC-2026-058 (P2) assigned to Maya, Joey, Ravi.
Sam (SRE): After patch: sampling back to 1%, fallback enabled. Early check: client 8432 errors dropped from 0.35% -> 0.02%. Fallback success 98.9% (some legacy mismatches).
Ravi: Captured a representative failure and opened TECH-502 for the model adapter to fix schema output (items -> object). Also filed a separate task to add a linter to prevent sampling misconfig edits.
Maya: Postmortem owners: Maya (timeline + impact), Ravi (instrumentation), Joey (router fixes), Sam (billing treatment). We also need a canary rollout checklist item: sampling, fallback, telemetry, example-scrubber, billing rule. I'll add to playbook.
Joey: Thx team. I'll watch the dashboard for 30m and escalate if fallback success < 98%.
Maya: Good job. If anything crosses 1% reject for prod routes we flip to P1 and roll back variant entirely.
Observability: status update pushed: dashboards live in console under fncall/validation; example stream scrubbed; metrics emitted.
DashBot: status update: INC-2026-058 resolved -> follow-ups created TECH-502, PLAY-119.
